audience.notes: Sophie and Marcus (Sydney, 30s, AUD 150K to 250K wedding) are newly engaged or about to be; they read this for style intelligence and to see whether we have taste and know what we are talking about. Alexandra (private client) reads for provenance, discretion and the idea of a commission rather than a purchase. Kayla (bargain hunter) should find nothing here for her: no 'dupes', no 'get the look for less', no price tables of cheap alternatives.

payload.search_intent: Informational and inspirational: readers want to see the famous rings, learn the cut, carat, designer and reported value, and understand which styles are in. A secondary commercial thread (how to commission a similar look) exists, which retailers exploit with lookalike framing; we answer it with a briefing guide, not products.
payload.angle: The sourced reference list. Twenty-five celebrity engagement rings across three eras, each with reported carat, cut, setting, designer and value (source, date, original currency and an AUD approximation), plus a one-line style lesson. Then the trends the rings add up to, how to brief a private jeweller for the look, and the part nobody else writes about: proposing abroad with a ring of this value, and the celebration that follows. The Wedded Wonderland difference is the trip and the celebration around the ring, planned end to end by a Wedded Wonderland advisor.
serp_gaps_to_win: Sourcing: no ranking page in any of the five markets names a source or date for ring values, and the figures contradict each other. Every value we print is 'reported', with source, date and currency.

Accuracy: common errors in the SERP (Mariah Carey's 35ct ring credited to Grace Kelly; the Taylor-Burton and Krupp diamonds presented as Elizabeth Taylor's engagement ring). A short 'how we checked' note builds trust and AI Overview citations.

Breadth across eras: retailers list 5 to 15 mostly recent rings. We span 1936 to 2025 with 25 entries, grouped by era like the strongest competitor (Carat Heritage), but with more entries and sources.

The proposal and celebration layer: no page covers where these proposals happened or the logistics of carrying and proposing with a high-value ring abroad (insurance, declaring, hotel safes, photographers, timing).

Australian and multicultural relevance: Australian connections (James Packer and Mariah Carey; Miranda Kerr; Nicole Kidman) and Indian celebrities (Priyanka Chopra) are under-used; 'celebrity engagement rings australia' and 'indian celebrity engagement rings' are live related searches.

Positioning: competitors sell lookalikes. We give a commissioning brief (what to ask a jeweller: ratio, certificate, setting, metal, lead time), which suits an AUD 150K+ reader and repels the bargain hunter.
FAQ and structure: only two of the readable pages have an FAQ. Add a 5-question FAQ (FAQ schema) and a comparison table for scanning on mobile.

outline.answers: Which cuts, settings and metals keep coming back, and which are new?
must_include: A compact table: trend, the rings that show it, what to ask for (e.g. elongated cushion, east-west setting, oval solitaire on yellow gold, toi et moi, bezel, coloured stones, emerald cut, old mine cut).
Short glossary for terms on first use: old mine cut, east-west, toi et moi, bezel, cigar band, three-stone.

outline.h2: How to get the look: briefing a jeweller for a celebrity-inspired ring
outline.answers: If I love one of these rings, how do I commission something like it without copying it?
must_include: What to bring to a private jeweller: reference images, length-to-width ratio, centre stone shape and size range, setting height for daily wear, metal, band width.
Ask for a grading report from an independent laboratory (e.g. GIA) and what it covers; natural versus laboratory-grown stated plainly without judgement.
Realistic lead times for a commissioned ring (researcher to source a range or mark NEEDS).
Link to our engagement ring budget guide for spend; do not quote ring prices of our own.
Make it personal, not a replica: the style lesson is the shape and proportion, not the logo.

outline.h2: The part you don't see: proposing abroad with a ring like this
outline.answers: We want to propose on a trip, like several of these couples did. What has to be handled?
must_include: INVISIBLE WORK SECTION. Insuring the ring for overseas travel before it leaves home (check the policy covers the destination and travel).

Carrying it: hand luggage only, keep the receipt and grading report, declaring high-value goods where required (researcher: cite Australian Border Force for returning to Australia and the destination's customs page; mark NEEDS if not found).

On arrival: hotel or villa safe, a private setting booked and held, a photographer briefed to be discreet, a wet-weather or crowd plan B for the chosen spot, and timing around sunset and local closing hours.
Two or three verified celebrity proposals abroad as illustration (e.g. Serena Williams in Rome, Hailey Bieber in the Bahamas: researcher to verify), never as our clients.

How a Wedded Wonderland advisor plans the proposal trip as part of travel: suite, private dinner, photographer, and Wonderland Benefits at partner, preferred and consortia properties where eligible (benefits vary by hotel and by program).
Soft CTA sentence here.

outline.h2: After the yes: from proposal trip to the celebration
outline.answers: What comes next, and how do the engagement and a destination wedding connect?
must_include: Short bridge: engagement party, choosing a destination, the wedding itself; link destination packages and the destination wedding planning page.

Wedded World Melbourne, 1 Hotel Melbourne, 7 and 8 November 2026, as a place to meet jewellers' peers, planners and venues: only if the article publishes before 8 November 2026, otherwise link /wedded-world.
Keep to 120 to 180 words; this is a bridge, not a second article.

entry_template.format: H3: '<n>. <Celebrity name>' (no year in heading). Then a 3-line spec block and 60 to 100 words of prose.

fields.year: Year of the engagement (public announcement year if the proposal date is unclear; say which)
fields.stone_and_cut: Centre stone, cut, colour if notable; setting and metal
fields.reported_carat: Reported carat with source; if sources disagree, give the range and say so
fields.reported_value: Reported value, original currency, source name and date, AUD approximation with conversion date; or 'value not reported' (never invent)
fields.where: Optional: place of the proposal or the wedding, only if verified
fields.style_lesson: One sentence: what a couple can take from this ring (shape, proportion, setting, metal, story)

rules: Every number gets a claim ID mapped to a research fact.
No celebrity quotes unless from a verified, attributed interview; no invented details about the proposal.
Respectful tone on rings from ended engagements (Mariah Carey, Ariana Grande, Kim Kardashian): state it neutrally, no gossip.

payload.differentiation: No existing page targets the head term as an evergreen reference. The 2024 and 2026 pieces are dated news round-ups of recent engagements; the 2015 'How big is too big' piece is a short size list. This pillar is the all-time, multi-era, sourced reference with a style lesson per ring, a commissioning brief and the proposal-travel layer. It links down to the 2024 and 2026 round-ups (descriptive anchors such as 'this year's newly engaged celebrities', never 'celebrity engagement rings'). The shortlist deliberately excludes the 7 celebrities covered in the 2026 round-up and the single-ring trending pieces, so the pages do not compete. Recommendation for marketing (not a blocker): consider 301-redirecting the 2015 'How big is too big' page into this pillar after publication, and adding a link from both round-ups up to this page.

research_notes_for_researcher: Primary sources first: auction house results (Sotheby's, Christie's) for R01, R04; royal.uk or official statements for R05, R15; designers' own pages or interviews for R12, R20, R21, R27, R28; official engagement interviews where they exist.
For each value: source name, date, original currency, and an AUD approximation with conversion date. If two credible sources disagree, report the range.

Proposal-abroad logistics: Australian Border Force guidance on travelling with high-value jewellery and returning to Australia (abf.gov.au is a government domain but not yet on the approved list; flag for a human decision), and Smartraveller for general travel advice. No legal statements without an official source checked within 12 months.
Commission lead times and grading report explanation: use GIA (gia.edu) or another laboratory's own pages; domain not on the approved list, flag for decision.
payload.seasonality_note: US and UK demand peaks October to January (proposal season). Publishing in early November 2026 is ideal, and also allows the Wedded World Melbourne mention before 8 November.
